comment: Chips seen in remotes: on a board in a picture, or named in an FCC filing. By hand; a data sheet link only where the address answered when it was added.

chips.name: PCF7941
chips.text: A remote keyless entry controller with an immobiliser transponder in one chip: the board needs a coil for the transponder next to the transmitter. The filing of `M3N5WY72XX` calls the controller "STARC 2XL" in its block diagram; the chip on that board is a PCF7941. Its CPU is NXP's MRK II, whose instruction set KAT decoded ([MRK II instruction set](mrk2.html)); the firmware of the [Renault Koleos](renault_koleos.html) key, a PCF7941, was read and run with it.

chips.name: PCF7961

chips.name: PCF7935
chips.text: A transponder the ignition lock reads at 125 kHz; it has no part in the radio remote. Sold as "ID40" when coded for Opel.

chips.name: TDA5100
chips.text: An ASK/FSK transmitter for the 433 to 435 MHz and 868 to 870 MHz bands, clocked by a crystal.

chips.name: HCS361
chips.text: A KeeLoq code hopping encoder: a 32-bit block cipher with a 64-bit key, the serial number and the key kept in the chip. KAT reads its frames as [Microchip HCS361](microchip_hcs361.md) and as [KeeLoq](keeloq.md).

chips.name: HCS301

chips.name: HCS200
chips.text: A KeeLoq code hopping encoder. KAT reads its frames as [KeeLoq](keeloq.md).

chips.name: NXP `1A58000`
chips.text: The 20-pin NXP chip on the Suzuki TS002 remote's board, marked `1A58000`, `6979708`. The marking is a customer's, not a type KAT could look up.

chips.name: `B 89AN S1080`
chips.text: The 8-pin chip on a 1999 Renault one-button remote's board, marked `B 89AN`, `S1080`, `49004`.

chips.name: NXP `22A1509`
chips.text: The 20-pin NXP chip on a Valeo two-button key for Citroën and Peugeot, marked `22A1509`, `AZS5702`, `TnD3011`, `9221509` (read from a picture). The marking is a customer's, not a type KAT could look up. A 13.560 MHz crystal stands beside it and the board shows no other transmitter, so the chip makes the 433.92 MHz carrier itself.

chips.name: Motorola `ZC421689CDW`
chips.text: The 16-pin Motorola custom chip on an old VW flip key's board, marked `ZC421689CDW`, `734 778-00`, `2E30A`, `XLAD9927` (read from a picture). `ZCxxxxxx` is a Motorola customer part number, not a catalogue type. The board is marked `734 613-02`; its other side carries an S+M `R707` SAW resonator and a 2.00 MHz ceramic resonator, and the unit that holds it is Hella's (`HLO 1J0 959 753 A`). It runs the VW-1 scheme (a 24-bit LFSR and a UID obfuscation, no cipher).
